active_failures.condition: Continuous finite-area soft contact under held-out changes in material relaxation, local thickness or curvature, sliding speed or direction, and tangential loading, especially when instantaneous normal force and indentation are similar across physically different contact states.
active_failures.observable_failure: A calibrated instantaneous normal-contact representation can fit or regulate its nominal condition yet cannot uniquely predict the subsequent normal/tangential wrench, contact-area evolution, or feasible wrench capacity across those shifted states; documented examples show recovery mismatch for simpler memoryless models, area/geometry-dependent force and moment, and degraded performance outside the model's calibrated structure.
active_failures.consequence: An impedance selector using only the aliased simple state can choose stiffness or damping without knowing which future wrench/constraint regime it is acting in, so equivalence of the selected action and held-out safety/task outcome cannot be assumed.

active_failures.condition: Bounded nominal regimes in which measured-wrench feedback, scheduled/variable impedance, static uncertainty compensation, or one calibrated finite-area model regulates contact well, followed by a shift in geometry, relaxation, tangential capacity, or material not represented in the controller state.
active_failures.observable_failure: Strong simple comparators are effective within their stated bounds, but their evidence does not establish action-equivalence after the hidden contact condition changes: model-agnostic admittance is reactive to current wrench, the static GP prior confines uncertainty to a static output map, and the calibrated finite-area MPC omits relaxation memory and online material adaptation.
active_failures.consequence: Nominal success can mask the unresolved boundary at which the simple controller ceases to be decision-equivalent; adding modules or retuning without identifying that boundary cannot justify a new method or a minimal sensing/model claim.

operating_envelope.task: Continuous sliding or scanning of a rigid probe over a compliant finite-area environment.
variation_axes: speed, direction, dwell and loading history
tangential load, slip/moment-capacity proximity and disturbances
operating_envelope.fairness_boundary: Comparisons must hold data, compute, objective, safety constraint, sensing latency and controller bandwidth budgets fixed and must judge impedance-action equivalence plus held-out closed-loop outcomes, not model-fit improvement alone.

simple_repair_assessments.repair: Use conventional variable/adaptive impedance or gain scheduling driven by current force/wrench error, including the strongest model-agnostic admittance comparator.
simple_repair_assessments.coverage_boundary: Can fully remove the superficial failure 'fixed impedance does not adapt' and can regulate six-dimensional wrench in calibrated, sufficiently observable and bandwidth-limited regimes. It remains reactive to the current measured port signal and does not by itself resolve two contact states that require different future actions before their wrench errors separate.

simple_repair_assessments.repair: Retune a conventional memoryless nonlinear contact model or local estimator and optimize impedance within that calibrated model class.
simple_repair_assessments.coverage_boundary: Covers nominal regimes where the instantaneous variables form an adequate state and calibrated parameters/uncertainty remain valid. It cannot distinguish path-dependent relaxation or geometry/tangential-capacity states that are observationally aliased under the chosen representation; more tuning inside the same state cannot create the missing information.

simple_repair_assessments.repair: Use a known calibrated finite-area, local-geometry and friction-aware contact model inside conventional MPC without a new state-selection mechanism.
simple_repair_assessments.coverage_boundary: Covers regimes where the selected geometry/area/friction model is calibrated and sufficient, and directly defeats any claim that finite-area modeling alone is novel. It does not establish relaxation-history, heterogeneous-shift, component-minimality, or decision-equivalence boundaries and can remain wrong when omitted state changes future wrench capacity.

simple_repair_assessments.repair: Combine calibrated six-axis measured-wrench feedback, conventional gain scheduling, static uncertainty tightening, and a known finite-area contact predictor under equal resource and safety budgets.
simple_repair_assessments.coverage_boundary: This nearest fair combination is the required simple baseline and may prove sufficient over much of the envelope. The current formal evidence nevertheless leaves an explicit residual where two histories/material/geometry states are not separated by its state before an action must be chosen; stacking the known blocks does not determine which additional information is necessary, whether it changes the action, or where it is unnecessary.

residual_failure_envelope.condition: After conventional measured-wrench adaptation, memoryless model tuning, static uncertainty handling, finite-area modeling, and their nearest fair combination have removed nominal/fixed-impedance failures, the controller encounters held-out soft-contact states whose relevant relaxation, geometry/area, or tangential-capacity condition is not identifiable from the retained instantaneous state before materially different impedance actions are required.
residual_failure_envelope.observable_failure: Under matched resources, the simple representation either selects an impedance action outside the prespecified equivalence margin from a representation that resolves the condition and this difference produces a repeatable held-out safety/task consequence, or it cannot certify equivalence because the same retained state maps to materially different subsequent wrench/constraint outcomes. The residual expressly excludes nominal regimes where the strongest simple combination remains action- and outcome-equivalent.
residual_failure_envelope.consequence: Without resolving this residual, the system cannot know when extra contact information is necessary, which smallest component set is sufficient, or when added sensing/model complexity should be rejected; the accepted practical decision-value problem remains unanswered.
